By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
filed by the petitioners Harish Chander and Tanvi Pandey, with respect to the death of Puspha
Pandey, wife to Harish and mother to Tanvi, in a motor vehicle accident.
2.  The accident in the present case took place on 01.06.2019 at 03:30 PM.
The deceased Pushpa Pandey, her daughters Tanvi Pandey, Nidhi Pandey and the Harish Chander were travelling in a car number UK- 01-TA-2557 to Ranikhet.
Respondent no. 1 Amit Rawat was driving this car.
He was driving it in a rash and negligent manner, in a high speed and was also talking on his mobile phone.
When the car reached Katpudia Majkhali turn, Ranikhet, the driver lost his control over the car due to which the car fell down in a gorge.
Due to this accident, all the occupants of car were serious injured.
They were taken to a hospital in Ranikhet.
Nidhi Pandey was declared dead by the doctor in the hospital in Ranikhet.
Pushpa Pandey was also declared dead on the same day on arrival in a hospital in Haldwani.
The petitioners have filed this claim for Rs.25,00,000/- as compensation.

3. The respondent no.1 and 2, who were driver and owner of the offending car have admitted the claim of the petitioner whereas the insurance company - Universal Sompo G.I.C. Ltd. has taken the general defences.
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were Harish Chander Vs.
Amit Rawat & Ors

7.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.

8. Now in this case, the petitioner Harish Chander has examined himself as PW-1 and proved how the accident in the present case caused the death of his daughter Nidhi Pandey and his wife Pushpa Pandey and injured his daughter Tanvi Pandey and himself.

He also proved the criminal case record showing that the chargesheet was filed against respondent no. 1 Amit Rawat, the driver of the car for causing deaths and injuries to the occupants of the car by his rash and negligent manner.
He has proved the manner in which the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1 Amit Rawat.
He has proved that the accident in the present case took place on 01.06.2019 at 03:30 PM.
He, his daughters Tanvi Pandey, Nidhi Pandey and his wife Pushpa Pandey were travelling in a car number UK-01-TA-2557 to Ranikhet.
Respondent no. 1 Amit Rawat was driving this car.
He was driving it in a rash and negligent manner, in a high speed and was also talking on his mobile phone.

He asked the drive to drive the car Harish Chander Vs. Amit Rawat & Ors.
carefully and not to talk on phone.

sentences.text: When the car reached Katpudia Majkhali turn, Ranikhet, the driver lost his control over the car due to which the car fell down in the gorge.

Due to this accident,
all the occupants of car were serious injured.
They were taken to a hospital in Ranikhet.
His daughter Nidhi Pandey was declared dead by the doctor.
His wife Pushpa Pandey was also brought dead in the hospital on the same day in Halwani Nanital.
According to the petition, his wife Pushpa Pandey used to provide home tuitions and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
His cross-examination comprised of nothing except the suggestions that he deposed falsely about the facts.
He denied all those suggestions and admitted none.

9. The respondent no. 1 & 2, the owner and driver of the offending car had accepted their fault and the claim of the petitioner in their written statement and has not led any evidence to contradict the case of the petitioner.

The respondent no. 3 insurance company has also not led any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.
10.

Therefore, the evidence of petitioner and admission of the respondents no.1 & 2 and also the absence of any contrary evidence of the insurance company, it is proved by preponderance of probabilities that the petitioner along with the entire family met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1, the driver of the offending car causing the death of Pushpa Pandey.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of said death and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
11. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

12. In the present case, although, the petitioner who is the husband of deceased Pushpa Pandey has mentioned in the petition that she was earning Rs.20,000/- from home tuitions and he also reiterated this fact in his evidence affidavit but then there is no proof of it.
In case of the housewives who are not earning, their income has to be fixed on a notional basis to calculate the compensation.

Various methods can be employed by the court to fix the notional income of a home-maker,
depending upon the facts and circumstances of the case.

The court should ensure that while choosing the method, and fixing the notional income, that the same is just in the facts and circumstances of the particular case, neither assessing the compensation too conservatively, nor too liberally.
(Kirti & Another vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2021) 2SCC 166).

sentences.text: But as held in the case of Kirti (Supra) there is no fixed formula to assess the notional income of a house wife and the case has to be decided on its own facts.

Further, the constitution of India prohibits any discrimination on the basis of sex under article 15, therefore the notional income of the deceased wife can also be fixed at minimum wages, more particularly in this case considering her educational qualification as a graduate from Delhi University and she had also done some computer course and also considering the facts that she was the mother of two young girls.
Therefore, in this case the notional income of deceased Pushpa can be assessed as Rs.14,468/- at the minimum wages.
(See also : Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs United India Insurance Company Ltd. 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1441).

FUTURE PROSPECTS:
13.

Therefore, her age on the date of accident was 34 years.

Since the deceased Pushpa Devi was under the age of 40 years, prospects to the tune of 40% shall be added to his income in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157).

APPLICATION OF MULTIPLIER:
15.
The age of deceased was 34 years at the time of accident as per the petition and the aadhar card of the deceased.
Therefore, multiplier of 16, as applicable to age group between 31-35 years would be applicable.

CALCULATION OF LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
16.
The monthly income of the deceased has been assessed at Rs.14468/.
This means that the annual income of the deceased would have been Rs.14,468x12=Rs.1,73,616/-.
After adding future prospects at the rate of 40%, this yearly income will become Rs.2,43,062/- (Rs.1,73,616+ Rs.69,446).
After deduction of 1/3rd of her personal & living expenses amounting to Rs.81,020/-, the yearly income will remain as Rs.1,62,041/- (2/3rd of Rs.2,43,062/-).
Applying the multiplier of 16, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.25,92,656/- (Rs. 1,62,041 x16).

loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
